q: How do I calculate the emissions saved by moving to drip irrigation?
title: Drip irrigation energy saving per acre
short: Measure pump kWh for a season before and after drip on the same land, and multiply the difference by 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25. Drip saves energy by pumping less water, but the saving depends on crop, soil and how the system is run, so measure it.
audience: Farmers, FPOs and drip irrigation suppliers

ul: Meter readings or pump hours before and after.
The same crop, area and season for both.
Pump changes noted, since a new pump changes the result too.

p: Drip pipes and fittings are plastic with their own footprint. For a full comparison, spread the system's footprint over its expected life.
The saving shows as lower Scope 2 for the farm. Report it as a reduction against your baseline, not as a credit.

example.title: Worked example: 10 acres before and after drip (illustrative inputs)
lines: Before drip (flood irrigation): 4,500 kWh a season, metered
After drip: 3,150 kWh a season, metered
Saving: 1,350 kWh x 0.710 = 958.5 kg CO2 a season
Over 10 acres: 95.8 kg CO2 an acre
example.note: Readings are illustrative; use your own meter or pump hours.

senseible: Senseible reads diesel, electricity and fertiliser invoices into dated, fingerprinted records that support a farm or crop figure. Field emissions such as N2O and methane are calculated with IPCC defaults in your method note and labelled as estimates, not measured values.
